conflicts: His claimed title and the public record do not agree. He says Division Chief of the Accidents and Investigations Branch for about six years; the first researcher to look found him listed as Quality Control Branch Manager on the Quality Assurance Staff. The OMB Form 171 he supplied in 2015 reconciles the two by sequence, July 1985 to October 1986 in the Quality Control Branch and October 1986 onward as Division Manager of the Investigation and Evaluation Division, but that reconciliation depends entirely on a document that came from him.

He says the military told the FAA 'they were short on their tapes and they had to put them back in service, but it's only been 12 days. Now, the tapes were supposed to be kept for 15 days.' No opened record corroborates that exchange, and it is not among the itemised contents of the National Archives file.

label: John Callahan
narrative: John Callahan is the most useful witness the Disclosure Project produced and the reason is not him. The event he describes is one of the very few claims in this cluster with a large federal record that owes nothing whatever to Steven Greer: over 1,500 pages at the National Archives in Record Group 237, archival identifier 733667, containing the air traffic control transcript, the FAA's own forms, dated January 1987 interviews with all three Japan Air Lines crew members, Captain Terauchi's written statement in Japanese and in translation, and the FAA Alaskan Region's press release of 5 March 1987. That record exists whether or not Callahan ever spoke, and it was recovered only because John Greenewald kept asking for seventeen years after the FAA wrote to him on 27 June 2001 that the documents would be destroyed in thirty days. The asymmetry is the whole point of this node. The case is documented to an unusual depth; the man's claimed office is not. He says, in the Briefing Document and at the National Press Club, that he was Division Chief of the Accidents and Investigations Branch at FAA headquarters for about six years. The researcher who set out in 2015 specifically to confirm that found, in his own words, that only four references to a John Callahan at the FAA came up and that none of them matched the claimed area; what the public record showed was a Quality Control Branch Manager on the Quality Assurance Staff under the Associate Administrator for Air Traffic. The document eventually published in support of the claimed title is an OMB Form 171, a Personal Qualifications Statement, which Callahan handed the researcher himself in 2015. Its dates are consistent with the incident falling inside his tenure and they reconcile the researcher's negative finding with Callahan's account, so it is a point in his favour, but a form supplied by its own subject is not an agency release and this board does not score it as one. Nothing about that weakens the FAA file. It is why the case node beside this one matters more than the person node.
